verses.commentary: Marshal your troops, city of troops. Siege is laid. Israel's ruler struck on the cheek with a rod. Present humiliation. The king insulted. The military city besieged. Lowest point before highest hope.

But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, though small among Judah's clans, from you will come for me one who will rule Israel. His origins are from of old, from ancient times. The most quoted messianic prophecy. Bethlehem, not Jerusalem. Small, not great. Ancient origins: the ruler is not merely future but eternal. Matthew 2:6 cites this for Jesus' birth.

Therefore Israel will be abandoned until she who is in labor gives birth. The rest of his brothers return to join the Israelites. Waiting period acknowledged. A birth must occur. Then reunion happens. The gap between exile and restoration has a term.

He will stand and shepherd his flock in the Lord's strength, in the majesty of the Lord his God's name. They will live securely. His greatness reaches to earth's ends. The shepherd king. Divine power, divine name, universal reach. Security through proper leadership.

He will be our peace. When the Assyrians invade, we will raise seven shepherds, eight commanders. Peace personified in a person. Sufficient leadership to face any threat. Seven or eight: complete provision.

They will rule Assyria with the sword, the land of Nimrod with drawn sword. He will deliver us when Assyrians invade, when they march across our borders. The great enemy defeated. The invader invaded. Borders protected by offensive action.

The remnant of Jacob will be among many peoples like dew from the Lord, like showers on grass that do not wait for anyone or depend on man. Refreshing presence. Independent of human calculation. Grace comes unexpectedly, cannot be controlled.

The remnant will be among the nations like a lion among forest beasts, like a young lion among sheep flocks, mauls and mangles as it goes, and no one can rescue. Two images: gentle dew and fierce lion. Blessing for those who receive, destruction for those who oppose.
Your hand lifted in triumph over enemies. All foes destroyed. Victory assured. The remnant that seemed weak becomes overwhelming.
In that day I will destroy your horses, demolish your chariots. Military removal. Israel's own military capacity stripped. Dependence on God, not weapons.
I will destroy cities in your land, tear down strongholds. Fortifications dismantled. Trust in walls replaced by trust in God. Human defenses unnecessary when divine presence provides.
I will destroy your witchcraft. You will no longer cast spells. Magic practices eliminated. Occult reliance removed. God alone consulted.
I will destroy your idols and sacred stones. No more bowing to the work of your hands. Idol worship ended. Self made gods demolished. What hands create, hands cannot worship.
I will uproot your Asherah poles when I demolish your cities. Pagan worship sites destroyed along with cities that housed them. Comprehensive purification.

I will take vengeance in anger and wrath on the nations that have not obeyed me. Final judgment on the disobedient. What Israel experienced in discipline, the nations experience in destruction. Disobedience has consequences for all.
